message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I would not call this ECG normal.** The rhythm appears regular, around 70 beats/minute, but the chest leads show concerning abnormalities:

- **ST elevation across several chest leads**, particularly V2–V5.
- **Deep negative complexes and loss of normal R-wave progression in V1–V3**, which can indicate damage to the front wall of the heart.

This pattern raises concern for an **anterior heart attack**. A previous heart attack with persistent ECG changes is another possibility; a photo alone cannot distinguish these. Comparison with an older ECG, repeat recordings, and troponin blood tests are needed. [Clinical reference](https://www.merckmanuals.com/professional/cardiovascular-disorders/coronary-artery-disease/acute-myocardial-infarction-mi?media=full)

**If you have chest discomfort, shortness of breath, sweating, nausea, or faintness now, call emergency services immediately and do not drive yourself.** If this is a recent ECG and you feel well, it still needs urgent medical review today.

Was this recorded today, and were you having any symptoms?
